stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Moderna and Merck say their mRNA cancer vaccine cut death, recurrence by 42%
stories.author: Beth Mole
bullet_points: Moderna and Merck announced top-line results for their mRNA cancer vaccine.
The vaccine demonstrated a significant reduction in cancer death and recurrence by 42%.
This represents a major advancement in the field of mRNA therapeutics for oncology.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, indicating a focus on practical model deployment.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
Indicates the model is relevant to text-generation tasks within the AI ecosystem.
Categorizes the model under key technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to major AI frameworks like transformers and the Llama family.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for persistent AI agents.
The model is designed for complex, multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.31 achieves significant speed improvements for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Canva’s first AI image model plans designs before generating them
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Canva is launching 'Canva Craft,' a new AI image generation model to compete with industry leaders like OpenAI and Google.
The model utilizes a two-stage architecture that enables design planning prior to image generation.
This planning feature aims to provide users with 'greater precision, consistency and control' over the output.

stories.title: Meta’s AI could still scrape news sites, legal experts say
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Meta's recent changes to its business terms aim to curb AI training on news sites.
Legal experts argue the modifications are insufficient to prevent scraping.
Concerns remain over vague language allowing Meta to use content 'associated with your products or services'.

stories.title: The FCC is beginning to block gadgets with ‘foreign surveillance chips’
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: The FCC has gained the authority to block electronic gadgets containing chips from companies deemed a national security threat.
The FCC is exercising this new power for the first time, blocking two specific gadgets.
The basis for the block is the presence of 'foreign surveillance chips' within the devices.

stories.title: Disgraced eMudhra drops out of TLS business after using cert private key of 4
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: eMudhra, a digital certification authority, has exited the TLS business following a critical security failure.
The vulnerability stemmed from a flawed key signing process that allowed the creation of fraudulent web credentials.
This flaw effectively permitted the minting of valid web credentials for any arbitrary website.

stories.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
stories.author: Shuang Qiu
bullet_points: Introduces EpiSEM-Bench, a new benchmark specifically designed to test LLM agents' safety when crucial evidence is missing from tool responses.
Addresses a critical vulnerability where agents might execute prohibited actions even with benign user requests if safety-relevant facts are omitted by tools.
The benchmark comprises 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs across six different domains, focusing on evaluating safety boundaries and evidence recovery.

stories.title: VERA: A Responsible AI Dashboard for Assessing LLM Deployments in Light of the EU AI Act
stories.author: Jérôme Lebecq
bullet_points: Introduces VERA, a dashboard designed to help institutions assess the responsible AI practices of LLM deployments.
The tool provides a technical interpretation of the EU AI Act, structuring evidence across six principle groups and eighteen technical requirements.
It bridges the gap between technical measurement (via benchmark suites) and non-technical regulatory approval processes.

stories.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
stories.author: Shuang Qiu
bullet_points: Introduces EpiSEM-Bench, a new benchmark specifically designed to test LLM agents' safety when critical facts are missing from tool outputs.
Addresses a critical vulnerability where agents can perform prohibited actions even with benign user requests if safety-relevant information is omitted.
The benchmark includes 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs across six domains to evaluate unsafe execution and evidence recovery.

stories.title: The Geometry of Metaphor: Probing and Steering Metaphor Representations in Large Language Models
stories.author: Martha Lewis
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) internally represent the complex concept of metaphor.
It employs mechanistic interpretability techniques to find causal subspaces within various LLM architectures.
The study successfully demonstrates the ability to steer LLM outputs, both in classification and generation tasks, based on metaphor representations.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Clef, a 27B multimodal decision model from Cloudflare, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users have the option to run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud infrastructure.
This integration expands the capabilities of Ollama by adding a powerful, large-scale multimodal model.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection's open-weight model, Beam, is now available on Ollama.
Beam is specifically designed for software engineering, reasoning, and agentic tasks.
The model is offered for free for a limited time via Ollama Cloud.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the safe execution of AI agents.
The integration allows these agents to run within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses deployment and safety concerns for running local/cloud AI models.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free decision-making based on text input.
Decision models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary LLM interfaces with local, open-source model ecosystems.

stories.title: Etsy is cracking down on AI slop listings
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Etsy is implementing stricter guidelines regarding the use of AI in product listings.
The crackdown aims to reduce the proliferation of low-quality, AI-generated content ('AI slop') on the platform.
The policy change is driven by buyer feedback indicating difficulty distinguishing between human-made and AI-generated items.

stories.title: Spotify says yes, it is busting people for using Family Plan sharing too widely
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Spotify is implementing a new QR code verification system to combat unauthorized sharing of its Family Plan.
The crackdown targets users who are not actually residing together, addressing account sharing abuse.
Spotify co-CEO Alex Norström confirmed the initiative during the company's recent earnings call.

stories.title: PC shipments dropped over 20 percent in Q3 due to RAM price hikes
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Global PC shipments experienced a significant decline of 21% year-over-year in Q3 2026.
The drop in PC demand is attributed to ongoing price increases, particularly in RAM.
The slowdown is part of a broader market trend, as smartphone shipments also reached a 14-year low in the same quarter.

stories.title: Switch 2 security takes a hit as hackers unlock homebrew access
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: The upcoming Switch 2 console's security has been compromised.
The vulnerability stems from an integer overflow within the 'SmileBasic' interpreter.
This exploit allows hackers to gain unauthorized homebrew access to the system.

stories.title: Electric or gas? BMW goes both ways with new 2027 X5 and iX5.
stories.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
bullet_points: BMW is offering a dual powertrain strategy for the 2027 X5 and iX5 models.
The electric variant boasts a significant range of 450 miles.
The EV option supports a high charging rate of 460 kW.

stories.title: Samsung all but confirms iPhone Duo is goosing Galaxy Z8 sales
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: The unveiling of the 'iPhone Duo' is correlated with a surge in searches for Samsung foldables.
The article suggests that the new iPhone model may be negatively impacting sales of Samsung's foldable devices.
This indicates potential competitive pressure between Apple's new hardware and Samsung's foldable market segment.

stories.title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
stories.author: Meisam Razaviyayn
bullet_points: The paper addresses the computational cost of test-time scaling in reasoning models, where many candidate solutions are generated.
It proposes 'Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization' as a new method for thought pruning during inference.
The core goal is to balance solution quality and diversity while reducing the computational load of running all candidates to completion.

stories.title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah
bullet_points: Introduces METTA, a new framework for Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation in Meta-Reinforcement Learning.
Addresses the challenge of representing long interaction histories in RL agents, contrasting traditional recurrent and quadratic-cost transformer methods.
Aims to enable agents to adapt quickly to unseen tasks by efficiently managing task evidence.

stories.title: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
stories.author: Wenyu Du
bullet_points: The paper addresses the significant memory overhead associated with n-gram embedding tables used in modern open-weight language models.
Current models, like DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, utilize massive n-gram memory (e.g., 196 billion parameters) to boost performance.
The research aims to reduce this substantial memory cost while maintaining or preserving the performance gains provided by these embeddings.

stories.title: Causal Chain of Thought: Mitigating Attention Leakage via Context Isolation
stories.author: Martin Gjoreski
bullet_points: Introduces CausalCoT, a new inference framework designed to address limitations in Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting.
Addresses the issue where standard CoT justifications might be plausible post-hoc rationalizations rather than causal drivers of the final answer.
Mitigates 'attention leakage' by enforcing causal transparency during model reasoning.

stories.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
stories.author: Chen Wei
bullet_points: The paper proposes using cheap offline proxies to evaluate robotic foundation models, moving away from expensive closed-loop rollouts.

It introduces the Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH), suggesting that different modalities (vision, language, motion) should converge into a shared statistical model of reality as models improve.
The core research question investigates whether motion trajectories function as a modality that should converge with sensory representations in advanced embodied AI.

stories.title: Phase Transition from Random Features to Fully Trainable Networks
stories.author: Shijun Zhang
bullet_points: The research investigates a 'phase transition' phenomenon when moving from fixed random features to fully trainable neural networks for approximation tasks.
The study quantifies this transition by observing analogous behavior in training errors: initial rapid improvement followed by diminishing returns.
The sharpness of this transition is shown to be dependent on the degree of initialization mismatch between the network and the target representation.

stories.title: SpectralCanary: Embarrassingly Simple Low-Frequency Traces for T2I Dataset-Use Auditing
stories.author: Furong Huang
bullet_points: Introduces SpectralCanary, a new method for auditing if Text-to-Image (T2I) models were trained on specific image datasets.
Addresses the challenge where models can absorb dataset characteristics without reproducing training images.
Aims to improve upon existing auditing techniques by balancing verifiability, fidelity, robustness, and deployability.

stories.title: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification
stories.author: Sachin Gupta
bullet_points: Addresses the real-world business problem of costly misrouting in IT support tickets using LLMs.
Proposes 'cost-aware abstention' as a method to conditionally decide when an LLM should abstain from classification based on explicit costs.
Compares LLM performance (zero/few-shot) against traditional non-LLM classifiers on a large, public IT ticket corpus.

stories.title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah
bullet_points: Introduces METTA, a novel framework for Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation in Meta-Reinforcement Learning.
Addresses the challenge of representing long interaction histories in RL agents, contrasting classical recurrent and costly transformer approaches.
Aims to enable agents to adapt quickly to unseen tasks by efficiently managing and utilizing task evidence.

stories.title: Causal Chain of Thought: Mitigating Attention Leakage via Context Isolation
stories.author: Martin Gjoreski
bullet_points: Addresses a critical flaw in Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting: the generated reasoning steps may not causally drive the final prediction.
Introduces 'CausalCoT,' a new inference framework designed to enforce causal transparency in large language model reasoning.
The method mitigates 'attention leakage' by isolating context during the step-by-step generation process.

stories.title: BeNice! Closing Looping's Inference-Memory Gap via KV-Sharing
stories.author: Daniel Y. Fu
bullet_points: The paper addresses the memory bottleneck in looped neural architectures, where independent KV-caches grow linearly during inference.
The proposed method, 'BeNice!', tackles this by implementing KV-sharing across the depth of the recurrent blocks.
The research demonstrates that sharing the KV-cache from the final recurrence with earlier ones can be achieved without sacrificing model quality (KV-s).

stories.title: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
stories.author: Wenyu Du
bullet_points: The paper addresses the significant memory overhead associated with n-gram embedding tables in modern open-weight language models.
Current models, like DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, utilize large n-gram tables (e.g., 196 billion parameters) to boost performance.
The research aims to reduce this substantial memory cost while maintaining the performance benefits provided by these embeddings.

stories.title: Can an Agent Debug a Web Corpus? Agentic Auditing of Slovak FineWeb2
stories.author: Jaroslav Kopčan
bullet_points: Proposes using an LLM as a 'corpus debugger' to find failure modes in multilingual NLP datasets like FineWeb2.
The agent explores the corpus via a read-only API, generating executable tests for human validation.
Demonstrated effectiveness on the Slovak portion of FineWeb2, identifying seven issues across multiple runs.

stories.title: Would an LLM Match into a Residency? Uncertainty, Reasoning and Image Use of Open Language Models on the Spanish MIR Examination
stories.author: Aitor Almeida
bullet_points: The study investigates the reliability of open Large Language Models (LLMs) on the Spanish Medical Residency (MIR) examination.
It moves beyond simple accuracy to assess crucial aspects like uncertainty recognition, clinical reasoning, and image utilization by the models.
The research evaluates four different open-source LLMs ranging in size (8 to 27 billion parameters) for potential clinical deployment.

stories.title: Diffusion Language Models for Perplexity-Aware Black-Box Attacks
stories.author: Suhang Wang
bullet_points: The paper introduces diffusion language models for creating perplexity-aware black-box attacks against LLMs.
These attacks operate in a continuous-space latent Gaussian space, decoding prompts via a random mapping and nearest-token lookup.
A key limitation noted is that the resulting prompts are often unnatural and easily detectable by standard input guardrails.

stories.title: An Empirical Study of Recent Large Language Models for Knowledge Graph to Text Generation on Standard Benchmarks
stories.author: Antoine Doucet
bullet_points: The study empirically benchmarks recent Large Language Models (LLMs) against traditional fine-tuned encoder-decoder models for Knowledge Graph-to-Text (KG-to-text) generation.
The research uses both reference-based metrics and novel graph-grounded, reference-free LLM evaluations validated by human annotations.
Findings indicate that recent LLMs are becoming highly competitive, substantially narrowing the performance gap with established methods in this task.

stories.title: My clients explain automations in rambling WhatsApp voice notes. Now my laptop answers with an n8n workflow
stories.author: gartox
bullet_points: Utilizes Whisper and Gemma 4 locally to process unstructured voice notes.
Automates the conversion of messy client voice notes into structured n8n workflows.
Demonstrates practical application of LLMs for real-world, low-code automation tasks.
